_meta.indication: Acute treatment of schizophrenia in adults and acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder in adults

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled; compared asenapine 5 mg bid, risperidone 3 mg bid, and placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with acutely exacerbated schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in PANSS total score
pivotal_trials.result: Asenapine 5 mg bid was statistically superior to placebo on PANSS (p=0.007; change -14.4 vs placebo -4.6)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, fixed-dose, placebo-controlled using haloperidol positive control; compared asenapine 5 mg bid, asenapine 10 mg bid, haloperidol 4 mg bid, and placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with an acute exacerbation of schizophrenia
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in PANSS total score
pivotal_trials.result: Asenapine 5 mg bid statistically superior to placebo on PANSS (p=0.014; change -16.2 vs placebo -10.7); asenapine 10 mg bid not significant in primary LOCF analysis (p=0.068); haloperidol superior (p=0.034)

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational (61 centers), double-blind, randomized, flexible-dose, placebo- and olanzapine-controlled, parallel group; randomization 2:2:1 (asenapine 5-10 mg bid, olanzapine 5-20 mg qd, placebo)
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with manic or mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in the YMRS total score
pivotal_trials.n: Approximately 200 patients per active group and 100 for placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Asenapine statistically superior to placebo on YMRS (change -11.5 vs placebo -7.8; p<0.05); olanzapine -14.6

nct_ctgov.title: 3-Week Study of Asenapine, Olanzapine and Placebo for Treatment of Bipolar Mania (P07008)

pivotal_trials.design: Multinational (55 centers), double-blind, randomized, flexible-dose, placebo- and olanzapine-controlled, parallel group
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with manic or mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline to endpoint in the YMRS total score
pivotal_trials.n: Approximately 200 patients per active group and 100 for placebo
pivotal_trials.result: Asenapine statistically superior to placebo on YMRS (change -10.8 vs placebo -5.5; p<0.05); olanzapine -12.6

nct_ctgov.title: 3-week Study of Asenapine, Olanzapine and Placebo for Treatment of Bipolar Mania (P07009)

key_safety: In schizophrenia, most common adverse reactions (≥5% and at least twice placebo) were akathisia, oral hypoesthesia, and somnolence. In bipolar disorder, most common were somnolence (24% vs 6% placebo), dizziness (11% vs 3% placebo), extrapyramidal symptoms other than akathisia, and weight increased. Boxed warning for increased mortality in elderly dementia patients.
target_moa: Atypical antipsychotic; efficacy thought to be mediated through a combination of antagonist activity at dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptors, with high affinity for multiple serotonin, dopamine, and alpha-adrenergic receptors

boxed_warning.content: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs; SAPHRIS is not approved for dementia-related psychosis

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the Division decided there was no need to take this application to the Psychopharmacological Drugs Advisory Committee as the data are consistent with a typical second generation antipsychotic drug

summary.text: Standard NDA (505(b)) for a new molecular entity atypical antipsychotic; approved August 2009 for acute schizophrenia and acute bipolar I mania/mixed episodes in adults after a prior Complete Response letter (January 13, 2009). No advisory committee was convened, and no expedited designations are documented.

citations.quote: This new drug application provides for the use of Saphris (asenapine) Sublingual Tablets for the acute treatment of schizophrenia in adults and the acute treatment of manic or mixed episodes associated with Bipolar I Disorder in adults.
The February 12, 2009 submission constituted a complete response to our January 13, 2009 action letter.
It was decided by Dr. Laughren that there was no need to take this application to the PDAC in terms of the clinical data, which are consistent with a typical second generation antipsychotic drug.

requirement.text: 1496-5: Conduct an adequate and well-controlled long-term maintenance study to evaluate efficacy and safety of asenapine in adults with acute manic or mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder

citations.quote: 1496-5 To conduct an adequate and well-controlled long-term maintenance study to evaluate the efficacy and safety of asenapine in the treatment of adults with acute manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder. The maintenance study should be appropriately designed to assess the efficacy of asenapine in preventing all types of mood episodes associated with bipolar disorder (depression, mania, and mixed episodes).

requirement.text: 1496-6: Further characterize utilization of asenapine in adults with acute manic/mixed episodes of bipolar I disorder with a dose lower than 10 mg twice daily (e.g. 5 mg bid) in an adequate and well controlled trial

citations.quote: 1496-6 It is not apparent from the studies you have conducted in bipolar mania that the lowest effective dose of asenapine has been identified. We request that you further characterize the utilization of asenapine in the treatment of adults with acute manic or mixed episodes associated with bipolar I disorder with a dose lower than 10 mg twice daily (e.g. 5 mg twice daily) through an adequate and well controlled trial.

citations.quote: Your submission dated August 29 2008, included the previously requested information on the rat and mouse carcinogenicity studies. Our review and evaluation of these data will be completed within the next cycle of the NDA.
- Provide levels of amorphous material in all the clinical batches, including the batches used in BE studies (Batch #AN and AT).

Please submit revised draft labeling for the drug. Please review and make changes according to the recommendations contained in the enclosed printed labeling. To facilitate review of your submission, provide a highlighted or marked-up copy that shows the changes.
